la forme co.

/la fɔʁm/

The physical outline or the overall condition of a body or object.

a dining room on the henley foreshore.

La forme co. is a minimalist and health-conscious dine-in restaurant. Being based in Adelaide, the business strategically caters to a locally underserved luxury-wellness niche; achieved through location, setting and a locally sourced menu.

after dark, eating well and going out rarely meet.

“Not always an option to eat healthy especially if I have somewhere to be.”

respondent, female, 25 and under SV-A

Henley already sells bowls and matcha by day. The brunch cafe closes at 14:30, the bowl bar stops online orders at 18:55, and one acai counter lists 21:00 on Mondays.

Dinner on the square runs from oysters and steak to Mexican, Italian and pub menus, and no guide calls any of it health-led. The choice is a bowl before seven or the night out.

matcha by day.

One room runs two services. By day the bar serves matcha. By sunset, the kitchen serves dinner.

dinner by night.

The day bar makes la forme co. a habit. Dinner turns the habit into an occasion.

the market.

Young Australians eat out more than any other age group. The core market is women in their twenties who train, eat well and share where they go; reformer before work, a run club on Sunday, matcha after.

They choose a venue on how it looks first, then on whether the food holds up. La forme co. is built to win on both.

the look.

The aesthetic is built slowly; warm, low light replaces the downlights, and nothing on the walls takes away from the presentation of the dishes.

The menu follows seasonality and a short supply chain. Every dish is plated for visual presentation; the images on Instagram are exactly what's served.

taste.

11 of 22

young women surveyed ranked taste first SV-A

Half of young women surveyed ranked taste as the most essential part of a dish. Three ranked health first.

Health is the standard in the kitchen; taste is what brings people back. Every dish is built on flavour first, then balanced for macros, with produce picked at its peak and cooked simply enough to let it show.

growth.

Post la forme co. to your story and the bill comes down. Every share brings in new customers for the cost of a margin point.

Adelaide micro-influencers are invited before opening, alongside food writers. After that, the service speaks for itself.

the brand.

Low light, friendly staff, beautiful plates, and produce sourced so precisely that nothing else tastes the same.

Luxury here is quiet. Linen, stoneware and glassware chosen for their weight in the hand; service that is warm without hovering; music kept low enough to talk over. The atmosphere is controlled by small variables, every one deliberate.

“people are interested in places that are photo worthy”

respondent, female, 25 and under SV-B

spencer gulf kingfish, barley, cucumber and goat curd.

Steamed yellowtail kingfish over pearl barley, with cucumber, cherry tomato, cos and fennel, Adelaide Hills goat curd, roasted almonds and a Kangaroo Island honey and lemon dressing.

sourcing.

The kingfish is hatched at Arno Bay, the curd is made in the Adelaide Hills, the leaves come from protected cropping on the Northern Adelaide Plains, and the honey from Kangaroo Island, protected for its Ligurian bees since 1885.

The kitchen cooks in olive oil, never canola or cottonseed.

Every supplier signs a non-GM declaration. Macros are published online and printed on the menu. S45 S54 S55 S57

from the gulf to the pass, step by step.

Six steps from grower to plate, with a check at each one.

01

grower

Harvested or landed to order, chilled at source.

02

market

Small produce consolidated at the Central Market.

03

cold chain

Chilled to the kitchen by the next morning.

04

receival

Checked against the supplier's declaration of origin and non-GM status.

05

mise en place

Cut and portioned for the day's two services.

06

the pass

Weighed and plated to spec.

A short chain means fresher produce, less handling and a clear answer whenever a guest asks where something came from.

Matcha is the one ingredient that travels. It comes from Japan, and the menu says so.

marketing.

Studios and run clubs are the most direct line to the market. Partner members get 10% off a matcha or a bowl.

Partner studios get first access to ticketed evenings. Each one brings a community that already trains together and already posts.

henley beach, facing west.

An $8.4 million upgrade around 2016 joined the square to the beach and the promenade, and the jetty runs straight out from it.

Henley has already established matcha's presence, with customers already aligned with the brand's values. Henley is casual, social and made to be photographed.

By day, not drinking is normal here. The run clubs and reformer studio on this strip would have a table after the session; none is a partner yet.

A new matcha counter draws trade from the cafes already here, so la forme co. competes on dinner, never on price. Takeaway is a litter risk; dine-in is on stoneware.

Evenings bring more people to the square. Dinner is seated, with last orders before the late bars.

award wages rose 4.75% in july. the roster is costed at them.

  1. political

    Licensed outdoor chairs cost $88 each a year by council permit. Police may start their summer operation early; dinner stays seated and food-led. S77 S26 S79 S42

  2. economic

    2,078 food and accommodation companies went insolvent in 2025-26. The plan holds two months' working capital (planning estimate). S76 MODEL

  3. social

    Japan's green tea exports to Australia rose 131% from January to August 2025. The day bar builds on it. S67

  4. technological

    DoorDash takes 30% of a delivery order; delivery prices carry it. S50

  5. legal

    A restaurant liquor licence ($730 to apply) makes meals the main service. Dinner is licensed that way. S81

  6. environmental

    Since September 2024, SA bans plastic takeaway cups and bowls unless certified compostable. Every one here is. S83

  7. ethical

    Fair Work found 79% of 36 venues checked in Adelaide's west broke workplace law. Staff here are paid to the award, weekends included. A discount for a post says so, as the ACCC requires. Marketing shows the food and the room, never bodies. S85 S82 S87

    Only 6 of 28 respondents rate ethical responsibility as important, so la forme co. treats it as conduct. SV-B
